info.title: OneNexus Central Auth Service — Support API
info.description: Support-team JSON RPC operations under `/support-api/*`. OAuth 2.1 / OIDC protocol endpoints under `/connect/*` are documented separately by their respective specs and the OIDC discovery document at `/.well-known/openid-configuration`.

post.summary:
Describe the first-party default S3 account and whether it has been
provisioned yet.

200.description:
Default-account configuration plus the live account

post.summary:
Provision the first-party default S3 account and its account-root user.
Idempotent on the account: if it already exists the existing account is
returned and the root user is not (re)created.

200.description:
Account provisioned (or already present). The root
    user's secret key is present only when freshly created — persist it.

409.description: A conflicting RGW resource already exists.

post.summary:
Page across all tenants known to CAS. Platform-admin / support
surface — there is no tenant scoping, this returns rows for every
tenant the caller is authorized to see.
post.description:
Ordering + pagination. Bidirectional cursor pagination on
the Tenant.Id UUID v7 PK. Forward (after) and
backward (before) directions both resolve to an index
range scan on the PK b-tree with no OFFSET cost. Items are
always returned in tenantId ascending order regardless of
direction — backward pages are reversed server-side. Because the
PK is UUID v7 (time-ordered), this is also a chronological listing
for free.
    Authorization. The class-level PlatformSupport policy
requires an active administrator of the reserved OneNexus platform
tenant. CAS resolves this from the current authorization store, so a
token does not retain access after an administrator role is removed.

requestBody.description:
Request body. Use `limit` with either
    `before` or `after` for bidirectional cursor pagination.

200.description:
Page of tenant snapshots. Body is a
    ListTenantsResponse; `after` is null on the last
    page and `before` is null on the first page.

400.description:
Validation failure
    (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/invalid-argument`) — typically
    a `limit` outside 1..200, conflicting cursors, or a malformed
    `before`/`after` cursor.

post.summary:
Page across the users belonging to a specific tenant. Platform-admin /
support surface — the target tenant is identified by Guid in the
request body, not inferred from the caller's principal.
post.description:
Ordering + pagination. Same shape as Task<IActionResult> TenantController.ListTenants(ListTenantsRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
but on the Users table, filtered to a single tenant. The
WHERE TenantId = ? AND Id > ? predicate rides the leading
column of the composite IX_Users_TenantId_NormalizedEmail
index for the tenant filter and the PK for the cursor bound.
    Tenant status is NOT a precondition. Listing the users of a
suspended or soft-deleted tenant is a legitimate operator use case
(audit, cleanup, recovery). Only a missing tenant returns 404; a
tenant that exists but is non-active still serves its user list.
    Authorization. The class-level PlatformSupport policy
requires an active administrator of the reserved OneNexus platform
tenant. CAS resolves this from the current authorization store, so a
token does not retain access after an administrator role is removed.

requestBody.description:
Request body. Same cursor + limit conventions as
    Task<IActionResult> TenantController.ListTenants(ListTenantsRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken), plus the tenant's Guid PK as `tenantId`.

200.description:
Page of user snapshots. Body is a
    ListTenantUsersResponse; `before`/`after`
    are null at the corresponding ends of the result set.

400.description:
Validation failure (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/invalid-argument`) —
    typically a malformed cursor, both cursors supplied at once, an empty
    `tenantId`, or a `limit` outside 1..200.

post.summary:
Add a roleless user to an existing active tenant. Role grants are
separate authorization-administration operations.
post.description:
Authorization. The caller must be an active human
TenantAdmin of the reserved platform tenant. This is the
implemented operator gate until a distinct platform_admin
authorization contract exists.
    Differs from TenantUserController.CreateUser in that
the target tenant comes from the request body, not the caller's
principal. The downstream invitation logic is identical and runs
through IInvitationService.

requestBody.description:
Request body. Validated by
    `[ApiController]` before this action runs.

200.description:
User created; invitation queued. Body is
    CreateUserResponse.

409.description:
The target tenant doesn't exist or is not
    active (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/failed-precondition`), or a user with that email
    already exists in the tenant (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/already-exists`).

tenantId.description: Guid PK of the tenant the user is being added to.

email.description:
Email address. Must be a syntactically valid RFC 5322-ish address.
Uniqueness is enforced per-tenant via the
`(TenantId, NormalizedEmail)` composite index, not globally.

displayName.description: Display name shown in UIs. 1–200 chars.

attributes.description: Entity attributes keyed by their Cedar attribute name.

tags.description: Native Cedar tags keyed by tag name.

CedarDiagnosticEntity.description:
One entity supplied to Cedar for a privileged support authorization
evaluation. The list is the dynamic entity slice CAS passes to Cedar: the
evaluated principal, resource, and every relationship entity needed by the
decision. Cedar derives static action entities from its packaged schema,
so they are not repeated here.

type.description: The Cedar entity type, such as `CAS::Role`.

id.description: The entity identifier within string CedarDiagnosticEntityUid.Type.

CedarDiagnosticEntityUid.description: A Cedar entity identifier, represented as its type and ID parts.

CedarDiagnosticValue.description:
A Cedar value in the diagnostic entity graph. The `kind` discriminator
selects the concrete shape: `boolean`, `long`, `string`,
`entity`, `set`, `record`, or `extension`.

function.description: The Cedar extension function, such as `ip` or `datetime`.

value.description: The extension value's canonical Cedar text representation.

CedarDiagnosticValueCedarDiagnosticLongV.description: A Cedar signed 64-bit integer diagnostic value.

fields.description: Record fields keyed by their Cedar field name.

tenantSlug.description:
Globally unique, immutable slug that members use to locate the tenant
when they sign in (for example, `acme`).

displayName.description:
Human-readable display name (e.g. `"Acme Corporation, Inc."`).
1–200 chars. Not used for auth decisions; shown in admin UIs only.

rootEmail.description:
Email address of the tenant's root user. Tenant creation sends this
user an activation invitation and grants the predefined
`TenantAdmin` role before activating the tenant.

rootDisplayName.description: Display name of the tenant's root user.

tenantId.description: The tenant's UUID v7 primary key.

CreateTenantResponse.description: Wire shape for a tenant returned by `CreateTenant`.

tenantId.description: ID of the tenant to look up.

DescribeTenantResponse.description:
Wire shape for `DescribeTenant`. Identical to
CreateTenantResponse; kept as a separate type for OpenAPI
clarity (each operation documents its own response model).

context.description:
Flat JSON object of request-context facts. Values use their natural JSON
scalar representation; the packaged service catalogue supplies the
authoritative Cedar type.

cedarEntities.description:
The complete per-request entity list CAS supplied to Cedar. Compiled
policy text and policy-storage metadata are deliberately not included
in this privileged diagnostic response.

items.description: All RGW accounts known to the cluster.

limit.description:
Maximum number of items returned in the page. Defaults to
int ListTenantsRequest.DefaultLimit when omitted from the request body.
Must be between 1 and int ListTenantsRequest.MaxLimit inclusive.

after.description:
Cursor for forward pagination. When set, returns items strictly
after this cursor (i.e. with a larger Guid). Pass the
string? ListTenantsResponse.After value from the previous
response to advance one page. Omit on the first call.

before.description:
Cursor for backward pagination. When set, returns items strictly
before this cursor (i.e. with a smaller Guid). Pass the
string? ListTenantsResponse.Before value from the previous
response to move one page earlier.

items.description:
Tenant snapshots for the current page, always ordered by
Guid TenantSummary.TenantId ascending. Because the PK is
UUID v7 — a time-ordered identifier — this is the natural
creation-order listing, with no separate `created_at` index
needed.

before.description:
Cursor for the previous page. `null` when no earlier items
exist.

after.description: Cursor for the next page. `null` when no later items exist.

tenantId.description:
Guid PK of the tenant whose users to list. Obtained from a prior
`ListTenants` / `DescribeTenant` response.

limit.description:
Maximum number of items returned in the page. Defaults to
int ListTenantUsersRequest.DefaultLimit when omitted from the request body.
Must be between 1 and int ListTenantUsersRequest.MaxLimit inclusive.

after.description:
Cursor for forward pagination. When set, returns users strictly
after this cursor (i.e. with a larger Guid). Pass the
string? ListTenantUsersResponse.After value from the previous
response to advance one page. Omit on the first call.

before.description:
Cursor for backward pagination. When set, returns users strictly
before this cursor (i.e. with a smaller Guid). Mutually exclusive
with string? ListTenantUsersRequest.After.

items.description:
User snapshots for the current page, always ordered by
Guid TenantUserSummary.UserId ascending. Because the PK is
UUID v7 (time-ordered), this is the natural invitation-order
listing.

before.description:
Cursor for the previous page. `null` when no earlier items
exist.

after.description: Cursor for the next page. `null` when no later items exist.
